summary: Notes by Richard Watson on a phone call with Bob Kahn about the ICCC network demonstration. They cover the physical setup in a hotel ballroom, including a false floor, a partition for a movie on resource sharing, and tables instead of booths. Other practical questions are covered too.

eli5.summary: A person asked the organizer of a big show lots of questions about the room and tables, and wrote down the answers so others would know what to expect.

questions: what resources were demoed at iccc
subtitle: Detailed notes on the planning and logistics for the ICCC ARPANET demonstration.

tldr.problem: The ICCC demonstration required coordination of space, equipment, personnel and resources across many organizations, and details needed to be documented and shared.
tldr.mechanism: Richard Watson documented his phone conversation with Bob Kahn, recording decisions and plans about the physical setup, equipment commitments, staffing and documentation for the October 1972 conference.
tldr.outcome: A detailed record of who would be involved, what resources were committed and what challenges remained.

today: RFC 372 provides a detailed historical record of the logistical planning behind one of the first public demonstrations of computer networking, showing both the organizational complexity and the collaborative spirit of the early ARPANET community.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 372 documents a phone conversation between Richard Watson from SRI-ARC and Bob Kahn about the ICCC network demonstration. Watson records detailed planning information including the physical environment, staffing, equipment and timeline, creating a valuable snapshot of the demonstration's organization in July 1972.
sections.eli5: After talking to the organizer, someone wrote down the practical details about the big network show coming up in October.

sections.title: The Georgetown Ballroom and Equipment
sections.content:
Watson records that Kahn had arranged for the Georgetown Ballroom at the Hilton Hotel, about 3000 square feet with dimensions approximately 75 by 40 feet. A carpeted false floor would be installed, and a partition would separate an area for a continuous movie on resource sharing. Instead of traditional booths, tables would be arranged around the room, each holding one or two terminals with low 4-foot partitions to divide the space.

Regarding equipment, the TIP had never been tested with 64 terminals before, so testing was planned for July with the actual terminals to be used at the conference. Kahn expected to start testing in August to identify which terminals worked with which resources.
sections.eli5: The space would have a special false floor and movie area. There would be tables with terminals instead of booths. They were going to test all the terminals and the TIP machine to make sure they could handle all the visitors.

sections.title: Demonstrations and Personnel
sections.content:
Watson lists several organizations and individuals who had committed resources: UCLA (network measurement), Stanford AI (programs), Utah (Tony Hearn's Reduce program and others), SDC (natural language and data management systems), MIT (hardcopy devices), SRI-ARC, and others. Kahn had also contacted non-network sources such as the New York Times data base and Eastern Airlines, but had not yet secured definite commitments.

For staffing, Kahn expected many terminals to be unmanned, though manufacturers could station sales representatives. People from network sites would staff some terminals to demonstrate their programs. Both Watson and Kahn recognized the need for many network experts on hand to help visitors, though Kahn had not yet assembled such a group despite interest from potential volunteers.
sections.eli5: Many universities and companies would bring software to show off. Some people would be around to help visitors, though finding enough volunteers was a challenge.

sections.title: Documentation and Support
sections.content:
Watson records discussion of documentation and help materials for visitors. Kahn's plan included large signs in the hotel lobby directing people to the demonstration, signs inside explaining what was happening, a card with TIP commands and available resources, a brochure with usage scenarios, the continuous movie, and support staff on the floor. Watson and Kahn discussed coordinating this with NIC documentation and planning to meet the weekend of July 7 to coordinate the effort further.

Watson notes that ARPA had not set up a dedicated budget for the show beyond what contractors were willing to contribute as part of their ongoing research, making Kahn's task of pulling off such a large demonstration quite challenging.
sections.eli5: There would be signs, cards explaining what to do, a movie, and helpful people on the floor. The organizer was doing a lot without a big budget and was hoping everyone would pitch in.

references.text: Kahn, R., "Demonstration at International Computer Communications Conference", RFC 371, July 1972.
